project.name: Pitscottie
project.boundarySource: Resolved named-place location with a conservative strict settlement study buffer
project.researchNotes: Pitscottie is stronger than a bare hamlet but lacks enough practical breadth for a 60+ town marker. Strict-boundary score verified sequentially on 2026-09-02. Customer or informal parking is not presented as general public parking. The nearest council public toilet is in Ceres. The café and nature stop do not by themselves justify a town-map score.

touristAppeal.label: Minor Interest
touristAppeal.summary: Pitscottie has a genuine café, a Dura Den nature stop and two usable route propositions including a live Treasure Trail. With no verified public toilet, picnic area or general visitor car park, it remains a good specialist stop just below the main-map threshold.

features.fullDescription: Mid-late 18th century masonry bridge, built to replace Callange Ford, on new Cupar to Ceres road, in construction from circa 1736, to the late 18th century. triple-span centre of 3 segmental arches slightly higher than 2 flanking. Very fine ashlar work, diagonally droved, with horizontally-droved margins, chamfered arch arrises. No parapet. Pair cutwaters to E (none to W). Ashlar weathered differently to either side, of pinkish colour to W, grey to E.

features.fullDescription: Mid 19th century, H plan picturesque villa. Simple storey and attic, snecked, stugged ashlar gabled slated with projecting eaves. Entrance in projecting gabled porch on West side. South front has advanced gabled wings to left and right, that to the left has a canted bay, square to the right, both three light. Link wing has two gabled dormers at attic, two single windows at ground, that to right lenghthened to form french window. Tall ashlar stacks with plinth and cornice. Small single storey to rear roughcast addition to rear.

features.fullDescription: Mid 19th century, single storey gabled rectangle with advanced gabled coach-house at South end, coursed whin rubble with stugged ashlar sandstone dressing projecting eaves, slated. West front segmental headed coach-house to left then stable door, blocked as window, and door before advanced coach-house bay with segmental headed opening and small loft window over. Wall to forecourt: rubble with square ashlar gatepiers chamfered angles, pyramidal caps.
